title: Smart Shirt Garments workers protest a Lunar New Year wage deduction in Kampong Speu
location: Smart Shirt Garments factory and National Road 41, Kampong Speu Province (search-preview lead)
organizer: Smart Shirt workers; a union president is mentioned in search previews, but the union name and formal organizing role are not established.
participants_original: VOD English search preview reports around 1,000 workers; VOD Khmer companion preview reports more than 1,000. Both are search-only variants of the same reporting service.
threshold_50_evidence: Search-only VOD previews describe around/more than 1,000 workers, which would exceed 50 if accurate. The English body was blocked by an anti-bot challenge; the Khmer companion was not opened and is not independent corroboration. No numeric bounds are inferred.

start_date.summary: Search previews date the road-blocking protest to January 25, 2023; neither article body was read.

location.summary: Search previews place the workers at Smart Shirt Garments in Kampong Speu and report a block on National Road 41; body evidence is unavailable.

organizer.summary: Search preview refers to a union president and workers; the formal union identity and organizer role remain unverified.

demands.summary: Search preview describes a wage deduction tied to a Lunar New Year day off.

participants_original.summary: Search previews say around 1,000 / more than 1,000 workers. They are English and Khmer VOD variants, not independent reports.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Previews qualitatively indicate a crowd far above 50, but no body was read and no numeric range is assigned.

state_target.summary: Search preview says the union president asked the Labor Department to intervene in a private wage dispute. Whether this meets the original domestic-state-target rule remains unresolved.

end_date.summary: A search preview says workers returned to work after a same-day agreement; exact physical end is left unknown because the body was not read.

state_response.summary: No event-specific government response is established by the search-only previews; all response dimensions remain unknown.

state_target: Search preview reports a request for Labor Department intervention in a dispute whose immediate counterpart was the private employer; eligibility under the original state-target rule remains unresolved.
notes: This is a search-only lead, not a body-verified event. VOD English returned an anti-bot verification challenge at S001; its same-event Khmer-language variant S005 was not opened. Search previews say workers blocked National Road 41 and later returned to work after an employer agreement, but these details remain unverified. The employer was the immediate dispute counterpart; no government action or state response is established.
open_questions: Can an independent contemporary source verify the physical action, date, venue, and turnout?
What exact labor department request was made, and does it satisfy the official state-target rule?
What were the physical start and end of the action?
Was there any event-specific state response?

title: Indigenous communities seek input into draft Forestry and Protected Areas laws at a Phnom Penh forum
organizer: Cambodia Indigenous Peoples Organization, as named by VOD English.
participants_original: Around 100 Indigenous community members from across Cambodia, according to VOD English.
threshold_50_evidence: VOD English reports around 100 participants. This supports the threshold qualitatively but is approximate and rests on one opened news report.

start_date.summary: The opened article dates the forum to January 25, 2023.

location.summary: The opened article places the forum in Phnom Penh.

scope.summary: The article describes Indigenous community members from across Cambodia attending a public forum in Phnom Penh.

organizer.summary: The article names the Cambodia Indigenous Peoples Organization as organizer.

demands.summary: Participants sought more input into draft amendments to the Forestry and Protected Areas laws; coded provisionally as land_farm_issue.

participants_original.summary: The article reports around 100 Indigenous community members; this is approximate.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The approximate attendance of around 100 supports at least 50 but has no independent attendee count.

state_target.summary: The forum concerned draft Cambodian Forestry and Protected Areas laws, and participants sought a greater role in input.

event_form.summary: The report describes a consultation forum rather than a march, strike, or rally; whether it fits the original MM event definition is unresolved.

state_response.summary: Ministry representatives attended and one official said inputs would be discussed, but coding of event-specific accommodation is left unknown pending the original rule and event-form review.

end_date.summary: The article does not establish a physical end date.

state_target: Draft Cambodian Forestry and Protected Areas laws; participants sought additional input into the policy process.
event_form: public consultation forum; contentious-action classification unresolved
notes: The opened VOD article reports a January 25 consultation forum of about 100 Indigenous community members and policy requests concerning draft laws. The forum may be a public assembly making a state-policy claim, but the original MM definition and codebook are not available here; retain pending evidence. S004 is an unopened statement and S006 an organizer-attributed announcement whose relation to this forum is not confirmed; neither is counted as independent corroboration or attendance evidence.
open_questions: Does the original MM definition include a consultation forum of this type?
Is the organizer CIPO, CIPA, or a coalition, and how do S004 and S006 relate to the VOD-reported forum?
Can the approximate attendance be independently verified?
What was the physical end time/date and any event-specific state response?
